overall: The AG reissued OML 2026-27 and found the Planning Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law on its April 9 minutes, and declined to review the hearing-vote claim.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the Board approved April 9 meeting minutes that were not sufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons set forth in OML 2025-209, incorporated herein by reference, we find that minutes of the April 9 meeting were sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the minutes inaccurately showed the hearing was continued at 7:00 p.m. while the meeting adjourned at 9:16 p.m.
allegations.key_passage: Although the minutes might have been clearer if they stated that the public hearing was continued to May 7 at 7:00 p.m., the minutes as worded substantially complied with the accuracy requirement.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the Board failed to vote to open or continue the public hearing.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not govern the procedural requirements for conducting a public hearing.
